Apply a unified diff

Source: R/patch.R
patch_apply.Rd

Applies a patch to old, a string. Every hunk must match old exactly where its header says: its unchanged and deleted lines, endings included, must be the lines of old at that position. There is no fuzz and no search for an offset; a hunk that does not match is an error naming it.

Usage

patch_apply(old, patch)

Arguments

old

The text the patch was made from, as one string.

patch

A unified diff: one string, or the result of patch_parse(), or one file patch from it. It must hold one file patch, or none, which leaves old as it is.

Value

The patched text, as one string.

Examples

old <- "a\nb\nc\n"
new <- "a\nx\nc\n"
patch <- diff_unified(diff_text(old, new))
identical(patch_apply(old, patch), new)
#> [1] TRUE
